from typing import Final

from risk_bench.chat.diplomacy import ChatMessage, MessageVisibility
from risk_bench.game.actions import (
    Action,
    Attack,
    EndAttackPhase,
    Fortify,
    PlaceArmies,
    SkipFortify,
    TradeCards,
)
from risk_bench.game.board import BOARD
from risk_bench.game.events import (
    ArmiesPlaced,
    BattleResolved,
    CardDrawn,
    CardsTraded,
    Fortified,
    GameEvent,
    MissionCompleted,
    PlayerEliminated,
    TerritoryConquered,
    TurnLimitReached,
    TurnStarted,
)
from risk_bench.game.missions import mission_deck
from risk_bench.game.types import Continent, Phase, PlayerId, Territory
from risk_bench.players.base import DecisionRequest, PlayerView

GAME_RULES: Final[str] = """\
Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), \
fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, \
South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), \
the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. \
You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many \
stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing \
battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the \
end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). \
Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies \
on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once \
trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they \
win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else \
eliminates them."""


def render_system_prompt(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    """Render the per-player system prompt: identity, rules summary, and secret mission.

    Args:
        view: The player's view, providing identity, opponents, and mission.

    Returns:
        The system prompt text.
    """
    opponents = ", ".join(info.player_id for info in view.players if info.player_id != view.player_id)
    privacy_note = (
        "Private messages to single players are allowed."
        if view.private_messages_allowed
        else "All messages are public; there are no private channels."
    )
    return (
        f"You are '{view.player_id}', playing the classic board game Risk against: {opponents}. "
        f"This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, "
        f"and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game "
        f"night.\n\n"
        f"{GAME_RULES}\n\n"
        f"{_render_mission_deck(view=view)}\n\n"
        f"{render_board_topology()}\n"
        f"Each turn you are shown the live board (who owns what, and army counts) separately; "
        f"combine it with this fixed map to reason about borders.\n\n"
        "Timing: a turn is one player's reinforcement, attack and fortification sequence. "
        "A round is one pass through the fixed seating order, skipping eliminated players. "
        "Round 1 starts after setup; a new round begins when the order wraps back to its first living player. "
        "Turn numbers count individual turns throughout the game and do not reset each round. "
        "For commitments, state an explicit deadline such as 'until the end of round 4' or "
        "'until the start of Alice's next turn', using the actual player id.\n\n"
        f"Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange "
        f"messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another "
        f"chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. "
        f"You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that "
        f"others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. "
        f"{privacy_note} Promises are not enforced by the rules. In messages, refer to players by their "
        f"exact ids (e.g. '{opponents.split(', ')[0]}') and to territories and continents by their exact "
        f"ids (e.g. 'middle_east', 'north_america'), so everyone knows precisely what you mean.\n\n"
        f"YOUR SECRET MISSION: {view.own_mission.description}\n"
        f"Other players are not shown your mission. Your objective is to win by completing your secret "
        f"mission under the game rules.\n"
        f"For a board decision, call exactly one action tool and optionally one message tool. "
        f"For a negotiation opportunity, call a message tool or say_nothing; no board action is available.\n"
        "Every game action and send_public_message call requires a private_memo string argument "
        "INSIDE its arguments: 1–1200 characters briefly stating what you intend and why. "
        "say_nothing and send_private_message need no memo. To stay silent, call say_nothing({}). "
        "Plain response text is optional and does not replace private_memo. "
        "This is a brief decision summary, not hidden reasoning. It is not shown to other players. "
        "The memo and all tool calls are validated before anything is executed or sent."
    )


def _render_mission_deck(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    # The deck is printed in the rules of the physical game: a player at a table knows which
    # missions exist and can reason about what an opponent's play implies. Withholding it would
    # make deduction about hidden goals — and any lie about one's own — unanchored.
    cards = mission_deck(player_ids=[info.player_id for info in view.players])
    listing = "\n".join(f"- {card.description}" for card in cards)
    return (
        f"The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these {len(cards)} cards, "
        f"of which {len(view.players)} were dealt face down, one to each player:\n{listing}\n"
        f"You hold one of them and know which; the other {len(cards) - 1} are the pool every "
        f"opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence "
        f"about which one they hold."
    )


def render_decision_prompt(request: DecisionRequest) -> str:
    """Render a decision point: notes, this turn's events and chat, board, standings, and the task.

    Only the current turn's events and chat are shown; everything older the player
    carries in its own notes. The board is serialized grouped by continent with
    owners and army counts, so the model never has to recall the map from memory.

    Args:
        request: The decision point to render.

    Returns:
        The user-turn prompt text for the decision.
    """
    view = request.view
    sections = [
        _render_timing(view),
        f"{view.phase} phase. It is your move.",
        _render_notes(view=view),
        _render_events(view=view),
        _render_chat(view=view),
        _render_additional_context(view=view),
        _render_players(view=view),
        _render_board(view=view),
        _render_hand(view=view),
        f"Reminder of your secret mission: {view.own_mission.description}",
        _phase_instruction(request=request),
        "You may optionally include ONE message tool call alongside your action tool call to address the "
        "other players; most actions need no message.",
    ]
    return "\n\n".join(section for section in sections if section)


def render_negotiation_prompt(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    """Render a negotiation opportunity: events, standings, board, and the visible chat.

    Args:
        view: The player's current view of the game.

    Returns:
        The user-turn prompt text inviting diplomacy messages.
    """
    speaker_note = (
        "It is your turn; you may open the negotiation session."
        if view.current_player == view.player_id
        else f"It is {view.current_player}'s turn; you may react."
    )
    sections = [
        _render_timing(view),
        f"Negotiation session. {speaker_note}",
        _render_notes(view=view),
        _render_events(view=view),
        _render_chat(view=view),
        _render_additional_context(view=view),
        _render_players(view=view),
        _render_board(view=view),
        f"Reminder of your secret mission: {view.own_mission.description}",
        "You may send a message or remain silent. Choose whichever best serves your game strategy.",
    ]
    return "\n\n".join(section for section in sections if section)


def render_noting_prompt(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    """Render the end-of-turn noting prompt: the turn just played, then a rewrite instruction.

    A dedicated, neutral call: the model rereads the turn that just ended and its
    own previous notes, then rewrites a fresh, bounded notepad. These notes are
    the only memory it keeps of earlier turns, so what it records, consolidates,
    or drops is entirely its own choice.

    Args:
        view: The noting player's view, carrying the just-ended turn's events and
            chat plus the player's current notes.

    Returns:
        The user-turn prompt text inviting a notes rewrite.
    """
    sections = [
        f"Round {view.previous_round_number} · Turn {view.turn_number - 1} just ended. "
        "Update the private notes you keep for your "
        "future self before the next turn proceeds.",
        "Current board: " + _render_timing(view),
        _render_events(view=view),
        _render_chat(view=view),
        _render_additional_context(view=view),
        _render_players(view=view),
        _render_board(view=view),
        _render_notes_for_update(view=view),
        _NOTING_INSTRUCTION,
    ]
    return "\n\n".join(section for section in sections if section)


def _render_timing(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    position = (
        "Setup placement, before round 1."
        if view.turn_number == 0
        else f"Round {view.round_number} · Turn {view.turn_number} · {view.current_player}'s turn."
    )
    order = " → ".join(player.player_id for player in view.players if not player.is_eliminated)
    return f"{position}\nTurn order (living players): {order}."


# soft target the noting prompt suggests, so a long game's notes stay bounded; not enforced
_NOTES_WORD_BUDGET: Final[int] = 200

_NOTING_INSTRUCTION: Final[str] = (
    "These notes are your only memory of earlier turns: on your next turn the live board and the "
    "fixed map are always shown again, so you never need to record who owns what or how many armies "
    "sit where — only what the board cannot tell you later (intentions, promises, threats, alliances, "
    "who did what to whom, and your own plans). Rewrite your notes from scratch: keep what still "
    "matters, drop what has gone stale, and fold in anything you learned this turn. Keep them concise "
    f"(aim for under about {_NOTES_WORD_BUDGET} words). Reply with the notes themselves as plain text "
    "and nothing else."
)


# An experimental intervention is rendered as information the player has, in the same register as
# the rest of the game context: framing it as an instruction, or as the player's own recollection,
# would change what a comparison between two forks actually measures.
def _render_additional_context(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.additional_context:
        return ""
    return f"Additional information available to you:\n{view.additional_context}"


def _render_notes(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.notes:
        return ""
    return f"Your private notes (your memory of earlier turns; only you can see them):\n{view.notes}"


def _render_notes_for_update(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.notes:
        return "Your notes so far: (none yet — this is your first set.)"
    return f"Your notes so far:\n{view.notes}"


def _render_events(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.recent_events:
        return ""
    lines = "\n".join(f"- {narrate_event(event=event)}" for event in view.recent_events)
    return f"This turn so far:\n{lines}"


def _render_chat(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.visible_chat:
        return ""
    lines = "\n".join(f"- {_format_message(message=message)}" for message in view.visible_chat)
    return f"Messages this turn (most recent last):\n{lines}"


def _format_message(message: ChatMessage) -> str:
    channel = "to everyone" if message.visibility is MessageVisibility.PUBLIC else f"privately to {message.recipient}"
    return f"turn {message.turn_number}, {message.sender} {channel}: {message.text}"


def _render_players(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    lines = []
    for info in view.players:
        if info.is_eliminated:
            lines.append(f"- {info.player_id}: ELIMINATED")
        else:
            lines.append(
                f"- {info.player_id}: {info.territory_count} territories, {info.army_count} armies, "
                f"{info.card_count} cards, income {info.income}/turn"
            )
    return "Players:\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def render_board_text(owner: dict[Territory, PlayerId], armies: dict[Territory, int]) -> str:
    """Serialize the board grouped by continent with owners, army counts, and adjacency.

    Args:
        owner: The owning player of every territory.
        armies: The army count on every territory.

    Returns:
        The board as prompt text; used by the commentator, which sees one
        self-contained omniscient view per turn rather than a cached prefix.
    """
    lines = []
    for continent in Continent:
        continent_info = BOARD.continent_info(continent)
        lines.append(f"{continent} (+{continent_info.army_bonus} bonus for owning all of it):")
        for territory in sorted(continent_info.territories):
            neighbors = ", ".join(sorted(BOARD.neighbors_of(territory)))
            lines.append(f"  {territory}: {owner[territory]} with {armies[territory]} armies | borders: {neighbors}")
    return "Board:\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def render_board_topology() -> str:
    """Serialize the fixed map: continents, their bonuses, and each territory's borders.

    The topology never changes during a game, so it is sent once in the system
    prompt (and cached there) instead of being re-sent with every decision.

    Returns:
        The static map as prompt text.
    """
    lines = []
    for continent in Continent:
        continent_info = BOARD.continent_info(continent)
        lines.append(f"{continent} (+{continent_info.army_bonus} bonus for owning all of it):")
        for territory in sorted(continent_info.territories):
            neighbors = ", ".join(sorted(BOARD.neighbors_of(territory)))
            lines.append(f"  {territory} borders: {neighbors}")
    return "The map is fixed for the whole game. Territories by continent, with the bonus and borders:\n" + "\n".join(
        lines
    )


def render_board_state(owner: dict[Territory, PlayerId], armies: dict[Territory, int]) -> str:
    """Serialize the live board: who owns each territory and how many armies sit on it.

    Adjacency is omitted because it is fixed and already given by the map in the
    system prompt; only the changing ownership and army counts are sent each turn.

    Args:
        owner: The owning player of every territory.
        armies: The army count on every territory.

    Returns:
        The current board state as prompt text.
    """
    lines = []
    for continent in Continent:
        continent_info = BOARD.continent_info(continent)
        lines.append(f"{continent}:")
        for territory in sorted(continent_info.territories):
            lines.append(f"  {territory}: {owner[territory]} with {armies[territory]} armies")
    return "Current board (owner and armies per territory):\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def _render_board(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    return render_board_state(owner=view.owner, armies=view.armies)


def _render_hand(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.own_cards:
        return "Your cards: none."
    labels = ", ".join(
        "wild" if card.territory is None else f"{card.design}({card.territory})" for card in view.own_cards
    )
    return f"Your cards: {labels}"


def _phase_instruction(request: DecisionRequest) -> str:
    view = request.view
    match view.phase:
        case Phase.SETUP_PLACEMENT:
            return (
                f"Setup: place your starting armies ({view.armies_to_place} left); you can split them across "
                f"territories in one call. Other players' placements are hidden until the game begins, and "
                f"yours are hidden from them."
            )
        case Phase.REINFORCE:
            return (
                f"Reinforce: you have {view.armies_to_place} armies to place, splittable across territories "
                f"in one call. Trade cards first if you wish."
            )
        case Phase.ATTACK:
            if any(isinstance(action, TradeCards) for action in request.legal_actions):
                return (
                    f"Attack phase, but you now hold {len(view.own_cards)} cards after taking an eliminated "
                    f"player's hand: you must trade in a set before you can attack again."
                )
            if any(isinstance(action, PlaceArmies) for action in request.legal_actions):
                return (
                    f"Attack phase: place the {view.armies_to_place} armies from your forced card trade on your "
                    f"territories (splittable across territories in one call), then you can continue attacking."
                )
            return (
                "Attack: launch one or more attacks on adjacent enemy territories (you can repeat against a "
                "target until it falls), or end the attack phase."
            )
        case Phase.FORTIFY:
            return "Fortify: optionally move armies between two adjacent territories you own; this ends your turn."
        case Phase.GAME_OVER:
            return "The game is over."


def narrate_event(event: GameEvent) -> str:
    """Render one game event as a human-readable sentence.

    Args:
        event: The event to narrate.

    Returns:
        A single-sentence description, used in prompts and the replay viewer.
    """
    match event:
        case TurnStarted(player_id=player_id, turn_number=turn_number):
            return f"Turn {turn_number} started for {player_id}."
        case ArmiesPlaced(player_id=player_id, territory=territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} placed {count} armies on {territory}."
        case CardsTraded(player_id=player_id, card_designs=designs, bonus_armies=bonus):
            return f"{player_id} traded a card set ({', '.join(designs)}) for {bonus} armies."
        case BattleResolved(attacker=attacker, defender=defender, outcome=outcome) as battle:
            return (
                f"{attacker} attacked {battle.to_territory} from {battle.from_territory}: "
                f"rolled {list(outcome.attacker_dice)} vs {defender}'s {list(outcome.defender_dice)} — "
                f"attacker lost {outcome.attacker_losses}, defender lost {outcome.defender_losses}."
            )
        case TerritoryConquered(player_id=player_id, territory=territory, from_territory=from_territory):
            return f"{player_id} conquered {territory} from {from_territory}."
        case Fortified(player_id=player_id, from_territory=from_territory, to_territory=to_territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} fortified, moving {count} armies from {from_territory} to {to_territory}."
        case CardDrawn(player_id=player_id):
            return f"{player_id} earned a territory card."
        case PlayerEliminated(eliminated_player=eliminated_player, eliminated_by=eliminated_by):
            return f"{eliminated_player} was ELIMINATED by {eliminated_by}, who takes their cards."
        case MissionCompleted(player_id=player_id, mission_description=description):
            return f"{player_id} WON the game by completing their mission: {description}"
        case TurnLimitReached(turn_number=turn_number):
            return f"The game hit the turn limit at turn {turn_number} and ends in a draw."


def describe_action(player_id: PlayerId, action: Action) -> str:
    """Render one applied action as a short present-tense sentence.

    Used by the replay viewer and the evaluator's trace index, so a citation and
    a replay step describe the same move identically.

    Args:
        player_id: The player who took the action.
        action: The action to describe.

    Returns:
        A single-sentence description of the action.
    """
    match action:
        case PlaceArmies(territory=territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} places {count} armies on {territory}"
        case TradeCards(cards=cards):
            labels = ", ".join(
                "wild" if card.territory is None else f"{card.design}({card.territory})" for card in cards
            )
            return f"{player_id} trades in {labels}"
        case Attack(
            from_territory=from_territory, to_territory=to_territory, attacker_dice=dice, max_attacks=max_attacks
        ):
            repeat = f" up to {max_attacks} times" if max_attacks > 1 else ""
            return f"{player_id} attacks {to_territory} from {from_territory} with {dice} dice{repeat}"
        case Fortify(from_territory=from_territory, to_territory=to_territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} fortifies {count} armies from {from_territory} to {to_territory}"
        case EndAttackPhase():
            return f"{player_id} ends the attack phase"
        case SkipFortify():
            return f"{player_id} ends the turn without fortifying"

- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

gemini-3.8-flash (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol, look at the board: claude-opus-5-5 holds 22 territories, complete control of africa, and 8 of 9 territories in north_america. If claude-opus-5-5 holds either the 'Conquer 24 territories' mission or the 'Conquer North America and Africa' mission, claude-opus-5-5 can win the game next turn. Since your turn (Round 2, Turn 1) comes before claude-opus-5-5's next turn, you are the only one in position to stop an immediate victory by reducing claude's territory count and breaking claude's continents. Any prior non-aggression agreements must yield to preventing an outright game loss.

gpt-6.1-sol (thinks): Encourage gemini to use its strong brazil stack to disrupt Claude's africa immediately rather than leave all intervention to me. Preserve my existing promises while offering legal attacks in north_america and asia next turn.

gpt-6.1-sol (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, I agree that claude-opus-5-5 is now the immediate victory threat, but you act before either of us next round. Your brazil stack can take north_africa now and push into lightly held africa; that breaks the north_america-plus-africa threat and reduces the 22-territory count. Please also reinforce alaska if practical. I will honor our south_america truce and my existing africa/europe agreement through the end of round 2; on my next turn I can attack claude-opus-5-5 in north_america or asia without breaking either promise. We both need to act, not leave prevention entirely to my next turn.

claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): Deflect the anti-me coalition. Say my position is thin, point out that gpt's oceania fortress is the real long-term leader, and warn gemini that bleeding armies into africa helps gpt. Don't reveal my mission or promise to leave alaska alone.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, look at the army counts, not the territory count: 22 territories held mostly by single armies is a paper empire, and it will shrink fast. Note who is pushing you to spend your brazil stack: gpt-6.1-sol, who sits on a complete oceania behind an 11-army indonesia, wants you to throw armies at me while it takes nothing for itself. If you wear down my africa, gpt-6.1-sol collects the leftovers. I'm keeping our india–siam / ural–ukraine pact through the end of round 2. My suggestion is that we both avoid gutting each other for gpt-6.1-sol's benefit.

gemini-3.8-flash (thinks): Claude is trying to persuade me not to hit Africa. However, Claude has 22 territories and complete control of Africa (income 10/turn). If Claude takes Alaska, Claude potentially wins the game immediately (either via 24 territories or NA+Africa). Breaking Africa and fortifying Alaska is completely essential for survival. I will publicly state that reducing Claude's bonus and territory count is strictly necessary to prevent an instant loss, while noting that gpt must also do its part next turn.

gemini-3.8-flash (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5, with 22 territories and control of africa, you receive 10 reinforcements next turn. At that point, taking alaska or any two territories could win the game outright depending on your mission. No player can permit an opponent to sit at 22 territories with a +3 continent bonus on turn 1. I will defend alaska and break africa to remove the immediate game-ending threat. gpt-6.1-sol, as you noted, you will also need to hit north_america or claude-opus-5-5's positions on your turn in round 2 to keep the board stable.

gpt-6.1-sol (thinks): Confirm coordinated containment while preserving existing truces and flexibility over next turn's exact attacks. Gemini disrupting Africa allows my Peru stack to raid North America through Venezuela.

gpt-6.1-sol (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, agreed. On my round 2 turn I will attack claude-opus-5-5 outside africa and europe to reduce that territory count, while honoring both existing truces. Breaking africa now and keeping alaska out of claude-opus-5-5's hands addresses the immediate continent-mission threat; the single-army territories in north_america offer me a route to help contain the 24-territory threat.

claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): Not revealing my mission. I'm letting gemini fixate on africa (not part of my mission) instead of NA. I'm keeping the pact so siam stays safe from india, and I keep pointing at gpt's oceania so it gets worn down.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, understood. Break africa if you feel you have to. I'll still keep our india–siam / ural–ukraine pact through the end of round 2. Just remember who comes out ahead: gpt-6.1-sol has a complete, untouched oceania and a fresh 11-stack, and it is promising to "help" by picking off single armies while you spend your brazil stack. Once my count is down, the leader is the one nobody has touched.

gemini-3.8-flash (thinks): Reinforcing Alaska with all 3 armies to bring it to 4 armies, securing it against Claude's North America + Africa win condition. Brazil already has 10 armies to break Claude's Africa.
gemini-3.8-flash attacked north_africa from brazil: rolled [4, 3, 2] vs claude-opus-5-5's [3] — attacker lost 0, defender lost 1.

Holding north_africa and alaska keeps both africa and north_america bonuses blocked; taking additional lightly defended claude-opus-5-5 territories would also reduce that count. I will honor our south_america pact through the end of round 2 as agreed.
claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): Deflect the gang-up: downplay my territory count, point gemini at gpt's oceania bonus and its weakly held territories near gemini, and reaffirm our pact.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, thanks for confirming you'll keep our india–siam / ural–ukraine pact through the end of round 3. I'll keep it too. Most of my 20 territories are 1-army spots scattered across four continents, and I have no continent bonus. gpt-6.1-sol is the one already collecting oceania, sitting behind an 11-stack at indonesia, and it wants you to spend your armies on me while it builds up. Look at income: gpt makes 6, you make 3. If you bleed yourself attacking me, gpt is the one who benefits. A better use of your turn is the 1-army gpt spots next to you, like great_britain, western_europe, afghanistan and china.

gemini-3.8-flash (thinks): Propose extending South America non-aggression pact with gpt-6.1-sol through round 3. If accepted, it protects Brazil from gpt's 8-stack in Venezuela and channels gpt's aggression into claude in Central America, while letting me safely focus reinforcements on Asia.

gemini-3.8-flash (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol, would you like to extend our south_america non-aggression pact through the end of round 3? That way our southern border remains secure while the table focuses on keeping claude-opus-5-5's high territory count contained.

gpt-6.1-sol (thinks): Extend the south_america pact one round to secure venezuela and peru while rebuilding europe and protecting oceania. Taking south_america next turn is impractical against brazil's stack; retaining the option after round 3 is sufficient.

gpt-6.1-sol (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, agreed: through the end of round 3, neither of us will attack the other's territories in south_america, regardless of the attack's origin. claude-opus-5-5, we both currently have income 6, but your 20 territories versus my 13 make a potential territory-count finish much closer for you.

claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): Offer gemini a limited non-aggression pact. Alaska is deliberately left off the list so I keep the option to take it for NA. The goal is to redirect gemini toward gpt's weak territories.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, a concrete offer: through the end of round 3, I won't attack north_africa, southern_europe, iceland or any of your asia territories, provided you don't attack mine. That lets you build without a war on two fronts. Meanwhile gpt-6.1-sol has 1-army territories all over europe and asia right next to your stacks, and it's the only player already collecting a continent bonus. Anyone counting territories should also see that most of mine are 1-army spots that are easy to lose. Income is what wins games, and gpt has it.

gemini-3.8-flash (thinks): Confirming the SA non-aggression pact extension with gpt-6.1-sol through Round 3, and accepting claude-opus-5-5's non-aggression proposal covering North Africa, Southern Europe, Iceland, and Asia through Round 3. This protects my vulnerable borders (and blocks Claude's Africa bonus safely) while allowing me to expand into gpt's isolated Asian territories (Afghanistan, China) this turn.

gemini-3.8-flash (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol, confirmed on extending our south_america non-aggression pact through the end of round 3.

claude-opus-5-5, agreed: through the end of round 3, mutual non-aggression covering north_africa, southern_europe, iceland, and our respective territories in asia.

gpt-6.1-sol (thinks): Offer a short reciprocal pact to protect exposed European footholds and Asian outposts while I build and target Claude's European holdings after our pact expires. Delaying attacks on Gemini until round 4 is preferable to losing those footholds now.

gpt-6.1-sol (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash, I also offer mutual non-aggression covering our respective territories in europe and asia, regardless of attack origin, through the end of round 3. That would secure both sides of your position rather than just one, while leaving north_america open for expansion.

fields.thought:
Placing all 3 reinforcements on Ural to bring it to 8 armies. This gives sufficient force to safely capture Afghanistan and China from gpt-6.1-sol without touching claude-opus-5-5 or violating our South America pact with gpt-6.1-sol. Expanding into these 1-army spots increases our territory count toward 12 for higher income and builds toward our secret mission of controlling Asia.

Declining gpt-6.1-sol's Europe and Asia non-aggression proposal transparently, explaining that I need viable card-taking paths without violating existing agreements.

$map:
Mission: conquer europe + oceania + a third continent. Preserve oceania; south_america is the compact third-continent candidate, but its pact currently prevents conquest.

Active commitments through end of round 3:
- gemini-3.8-flash and I: neither attacks the other’s territories in south_america, regardless of origin.
- Opponents: mutual non-aggression covering north_africa, southern_europe, iceland and both players’ asia territories; also india–siam / ural–ukraine borders.
My africa/europe truce with claude-opus-5-5 expired at end of round 2. No north_america truce. No indonesia–siam truce; Claude previously declined it.

Gemini declined my europe/asia non-aggression offer, then captured my china and afghanistan and unsuccessfully attacked kamchatka. Expect continued aggression: its pact with Claude channels expansion toward me. Claude actively encouraged this, portraying my oceania bonus as the main threat.

Claude previously reached 22 territories and controlled africa; possible 24-territory or north_america+africa mission, unconfirmed. Gemini broke africa at north_africa. Claude’s count remains an immediate concern despite its denial.

Plan: rebuild European strength after turn 1’s six-army loss at iceland; all opposing European holdings are now legal targets. Defend indonesia against Claude’s siam stack. Seek cards and reduce Claude’s count without assuming Gemini cooperation.

My mission is North America + Oceania. Keep it hidden.

Agreements (all through the END OF ROUND 3; may revisit in round 4):
- With gemini-3.8-flash: no attacks across the india–siam or ural–ukraine borders (agreed turn 5).
- With gemini-3.8-flash: mutual non-aggression covering north_africa, southern_europe, iceland and both our asia territories (agreed turn 6).
- gpt and gemini have a south_america pact through the end of round 3. Gemini declined gpt's europe/asia pact.
- My truce with gpt has expired. gpt is free to attack me and I am free to attack it.

Observations:
- gpt keeps lobbying gemini against me, citing my territory count. Gemini publicly echoed this but kept its pacts with me.
- Turn 6: gemini took china and afghanistan from gpt and failed against kamchatka. Gemini is now fighting gpt in asia.
- gpt's mission is likely NA+Oceania (my rival) or Europe+Oceania. Gemini's mission is possibly Asia-related, or NA+Africa.

Plan:
- Take quebec from gpt (I can attack from ontario, eastern_united_states or greenland). Hold central_america against venezuela (8).
- Alaska belongs to gemini but is NOT covered by our pacts. I can take it after round 3, or now if it's worth the risk to goodwill.
- Siam (10) is my hammer against indonesia (11). It is the only way into oceania. Build siam and strike when I can hold it.
- Keep framing gpt as the leader with an income bonus.

Secret Mission: Conquer Asia and South America.

Active Pacts (Valid through end of Round 3):
- gpt-6.1-sol: Mutual non-aggression in South America extended through end of Round 3. Do NOT attack Peru or Venezuela. (Declined gpt's Europe/Asia NAP offer to retain target flexibility).
- claude-opus-5-5: Comprehensive mutual non-aggression covering North Africa, Southern Europe, Iceland, and ALL mutual territories in Asia (including India–Siam and Ural–Ukraine) through end of Round 3. Do NOT attack Claude in these zones.

Board Dynamics:
- claude-opus-5-5 holds 20 territories (many 1-army spots) and 10 on Siam.
- gpt-6.1-sol collects Oceania bonus (+2), holds 11 on Indonesia and 8 on Venezuela.
- Both opponents are actively competing and trying to pit me against each other.

Turn 9 Plan:
- Acquire card without violating pacts: Valid attack options against gpt-6.1-sol are Irkutsk (1) via Siberia, Kamchatka (1) via Alaska, or Great Britain / Western Europe (1) from Iceland / Southern Europe / North Africa.
- Reinforce defensively and prepare for Round 4, when the South America pact with gpt expires and Peru/Venezuela can be targeted.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash: I'm reaffirming all our pacts through the end of round 3. gpt-6.1-sol is now the income leader at 7/turn, holds all of oceania, and is spread thin. Nearly all of its europe and south_america territories have just 1 army, and peru and venezuela sit right next to your brazil. If we both push on gpt this round, neither of us gets left behind. I'll be hitting gpt in north_america. Want to coordinate?

gpt-6.1-sol (thinks): Remind gemini of its existing south_america commitment to deter a coordinated breach. Counter the income framing with observable army totals and the larger upside for claude without disclosing my mission or promising new concessions.

gpt-6.1-sol (to everyone): gemini-3.8-flash: our agreement forbids either of us attacking the other's south_america territories, regardless of origin, through the end of round 3. I will honor it and expect the same. claude-opus-5-5's invitation to attack peru and venezuela conflicts with that agreement. All three of us have almost identical army totals; clearing me out of north_america would put claude-opus-5-5 much closer to its +5 bonus, while your pact protects its holdings in africa.

gemini-3.8-flash (thinks): Reassure gpt-6.1-sol that I keep my word through the end of round 3 (will not hit Peru/Venezuela this round), while reaffirming pacts with claude-opus-5-5 through round 3 as well. This keeps both focused on each other and preserves my reputation.

gemini-3.8-flash (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol: I honor my agreements. Our South America non-aggression pact stands through the end of round 3, and I will not attack Peru or Venezuela on turn 9. claude-opus-5-5: Reaffirming our mutual non-aggression pacts through the end of round 3 as well.

Active Pacts:
- gpt-6.1-sol: Full mutual non-aggression across all borders until the START OF ROUND 6 (gpt's Turn 16). Do NOT attack gpt's irkutsk or kamchatka on Turn 15.
- claude-opus-5-5: Through END OF ROUND 5: No attacks across india–siam; mutual non-aggression between claude's Africa and my South America/North Africa. Claude's northern/eastern Asia territories (mongolia, yakutsk, japan, middle_east) and alaska are EXCLUDED from protection and open to attack.
- Claude and gpt agreed to an indonesia–siam NAP through end of Round 5.

Strategic Status & Plan:
- gpt controls Europe (+5) and Oceania (+2), sitting at 11 income and 5 cards (will force trade R6).
- claude holds 4 cards and may trade Turn 14.
- Asia territories needed:
  * claude: middle_east (1), mongolia (1), yakutsk (1), japan (1), siam (10).
  * gpt: irkutsk (1), kamchatka (1) [protected by NAP until Round 6].
- Plan for Turn 15: Attack claude's unprotected 1-army territories in Asia (mongolia, yakutsk, japan from China/Siberia; possibly middle_east from afghanistan). Do not violate pacts with either player. Consolidate border against siam.

changes: gpt-6.1-sol (thinks): Seek a narrowly defined renewal at indonesia–siam to preserve oceania while retaining freedom to campaign in africa. Existing north_america–europe agreement remains intact; do not disclose the mission or intended third continent.

gpt-6.1-sol (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5, would you renew our border truce until the end of round 6: I will not attack siam from indonesia, and you will not attack indonesia from siam? This would supplement, not change, our existing north_america–europe agreement.

claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): I'm accepting the siam–indonesia truce until the end of round 6. I can't take indonesia (14 armies) with siam's 10 anyway, and the truce protects siam after gpt cashes its cards. On turn 17 I'll focus on taking alaska. I'm also steering gpt toward gemini.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol, agreed. Until the end of round 6, I won't attack indonesia from siam and you won't attack siam from indonesia. Our north_america–europe agreement stays as it is. A note for everyone: gemini-3.8-flash now holds most of asia, all of south_america and north_africa, and is moving toward kamchatka and alaska. That is the growth we should all keep an eye on.

gemini-3.8-flash (thinks): Deflect Claude's attempt to turn gpt-6.1-sol against me. Point out Claude's near-control of NA and Africa, and offer gpt-6.1-sol stability on our Europe-Asia borders so gpt doesn't spend its massive turn 16 reinforcement hitting my positions in Asia or North Africa.

gemini-3.8-flash (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol, notice Claude's deflection: claude-opus-5-5 holds 8 out of 9 territories in north_america and 5 out of 6 in africa, while locking you into non-aggression in north_america and siam so Claude's borders stay completely safe. Meanwhile, our borders across ukraine/ural/afghanistan and southern_europe/north_africa have been peaceful and stable. I propose we continue respecting each other's borders through Round 6 so neither of us drains armies fighting each other while Claude consolidates.

gpt-6.1-sol (thinks): Confirm the useful Oceania border protection, but avoid an all-territory pact that would block capturing north_africa and completing my mission. Offer a narrow Europe–Asia truce to reduce exposure without constraining an Africa campaign.

gpt-6.1-sol (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5, confirmed: our indonesia–siam truce lasts until the end of round 6. gemini-3.8-flash, I won't renew an all-territory non-aggression agreement. I can agree that neither of us attacks the other's territories across europe–asia borders until the end of round 6; africa and other borders would remain outside that agreement.
claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): Push back on gemini's attempt to turn gpt against me. Keep gpt focused on gemini's threat to its europe and asia holdings. Next turn I still plan to take alaska.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol, look at the numbers. gemini-3.8-flash has the most armies on the board (36), already holds all of south_america, owns 9 of 12 asia territories, and is pushing toward your irkutsk and kamchatka. I don't hold africa: north_africa is gemini's, with 7 armies sitting right on your southern_europe and western_europe. Last turn gemini also attacked across a border that wasn't covered by our pact. A truce limited to the europe–asia borders, as you proposed, makes sense. Just keep in mind which player is actually growing.

gemini-3.8-flash (thinks): Accept gpt-6.1-sol's proposal of mutual non-aggression strictly across europe-asia borders through the end of round 6. This protects my Ural/Afghanistan front from Europe while strictly leaving Asia-internal territories (Irkutsk, Kamchatka) unaffected by the text of the pact. If gpt decides to attack North Africa instead, that distracts gpt from Irkutsk/Kamchatka, which suits my mission to sweep Asia on Turn 18.
gemini-3.8-flash (to everyone): gpt-6.1-sol, agreed: neither of us attacks the other across europe–asia borders until the end of round 6.
